result:
The api died at 03:14:06 because the disk at `/var/lib/stockroom` filled up, and it never came back: the proxy was still logging "upstream api refused connection" every two minutes when the log ends at 05:29:57.

The cause was the `report-export` job. Starting at 03:05:00 it wrote a 512 MB CSV into `/var/lib/stockroom/exports/` every 12 seconds, 40 files (about 20 GB) in all. The disk hit 91% at 03:09:03 and 99% at 03:13:30. At 03:14:00 Postgres failed with "could not extend file ... No space left on device", the api aborted its transaction, shut down its worker pool and exited with status 1.

Web and proxy kept serving 200s throughout. The `cache: slow command` warnings run at a steady rate from the start of the log, so they are unrelated noise.

To recover, free space by clearing or moving the `part-*.csv` files in `/var/lib/stockroom/exports/`, then start the api again. To stop a repeat, have the export write to a separate volume from the database, or cap or clean up its output.

The log doesn't show why the api stayed down despite `restart: unless-stopped` in the compose file; `docker compose ps` and `docker compose logs api` on the host should tell you.
